power.answer: South African Airways allows power banks of up to 100 Wh in carry-on baggage only, individually packed against short circuits. They may not be charged from in-seat power or used to power devices during taxi, take-off or landing, and must be stored under the seat, not in overhead bins.

sections.h: 🔋 What South African Airways says about power banks
sections.p: From the South African Airways page "Restricted Baggage Items and Dangerous Goods", sections Power Banks and Lithium Batteries, read on 22 November 2026.

head: Question
South African Airways rule
rows: Carry-on baggage only; never in checked baggage, and security may remove them
Maximum 100 Wh (the page names 27,000 mAh as an example guide)
Individually packed to prevent short circuits: original packaging, insulated terminals, or a protective pouch or bag
Do not charge power banks from in-seat or inflight power; do not use them to power other devices during taxi, take-off or landing
Under the seat in front or another designated place, not in overhead bins
Damaged, defective or recalled units; overheating, swollen or leaking units; any unit with smoke, burning smell or expansion
Carry-on only; up to two spare lithium-ion batteries of 100 to 160 Wh; 20 spare batteries in total, each protected
Wh = mAh x volts / 1000; the page's example: 10,000 mAh at 12 V is 120 Wh

list: Not on the page: the page does not say whether power banks of 100 to 160 Wh are accepted; it names 100 Wh as the airline limit.

faq: Can I put a power bank in my checked bag on South African Airways?
No. Power banks must stay in carry-on baggage and may be removed by security if packed in checked luggage.
What size power bank can I take on South African Airways?
Up to 100 Wh; the page also gives 27,000 mAh as a guide.
Can I charge my power bank on a South African Airways flight?
No. Do not charge spare batteries or power banks from in-seat or inflight power.
